intro: If your fridge is warm, you want a clear answer: is this a five-minute check, or do you need a technician in the Sacramento area today? Refrigerator-not-cooling jobs often fall into a few patterns. Some you can check yourself. Others need parts, tools, and a qualified technician. Below is how to tell the difference, how Sacramento-area heat can stress garage refrigerators, and when to book [refrigerator repair](/services/refrigerator-repair).

body.text: Fridge warm but freezer still cold

On some refrigerator designs, cold air is meant to move from the freezer into the fresh-food section. If that path is blocked, the freezer can stay cold while the fridge warms. Not every model works that way. Check the owner's manual for vents, a damper, or a separate cooling system before you assume air is supposed to travel between sections.

When a shared-airflow design is involved, possible causes include a defrost problem (ice on the evaporator can block airflow, and the fridge side may climb while the freezer still feels cold), an evaporator fan that is not moving air, or an air damper stuck closed. Frost on the freezer back wall, weak vent airflow, and a fridge that warms slowly while the freezer still freezes can fit that picture. Those signs are not a diagnosis.
Both sections warm

If the freezer and the fridge are both too warm, several parts could be involved. That symptom is not a diagnosis of the sealed system. Possible issues include dirty condenser coils (dust and pet hair under or behind the cabinet can make heat rejection harder), a condenser fan that is not moving air, start components that keep the compressor from running, or, less often, a failed compressor. A technician should rule out the simpler parts before treating the compressor as the cause.
Do not test capacitors, relays, or other electrical parts yourself.
Five-minute checks before you call

These checks are for safe, exterior or user-control items. Keep the doors closed as much as you can, and move perishables to a cooler with ice if you need time. Do not smell or taste food to decide whether it is safe.

items: Confirm the refrigerator is plugged in and the breaker has not tripped.
Check the temperature settings. Many fresh-food sections are aimed near 37°F and freezers near 0°F. Use an appliance thermometer if you have one.
Make sure interior vents are not blocked by packages.
Look at door gaskets for obvious tears or gaps. You do not need to remove the doors.

If the owner's manual shows condenser coils you can reach without moving a heavy appliance or opening electrical covers, unplug the refrigerator first, then vacuum loose dust. Cleaning accessible coils can help heat rejection if they are dirty. It does not repair a failed fan, compressor, or sealed-system part. Skip this step if you would have to lift, tip, or disassemble the unit.
From outside the machine, listen for the compressor. Some evaporator fans pause when a door switch is open, so a quiet freezer with the door ajar is not proof the fan has failed.

body.text: Why Sacramento-area heat makes it worse

Hot Valley weather raises the heat a refrigerator has to reject, especially in a garage. When the air around the machine is above 90°F, coils and fans work harder. Garage floors also collect dust. If a garage refrigerator struggles after a heat wave, dirty coils or a condenser fan problem are possible. That does not mean the compressor is dead.
Brand notes: Samsung, LG, and Whirlpool

Natomas Appliance works on major brands, including Samsung, LG, Whirlpool, KitchenAid, and Maytag. On some French-door and side-by-side models, ice-maker, evaporator-fan, or airflow symptoms can look like a warm fridge with a freezer that still feels cold. On some Whirlpool-family units, defrost heaters, thermistors, or dampers can be part of the repair. Brand is not a diagnosis. The symptoms and an inspection are.
Repair or replace?

Age is one consideration, not a cutoff. Repair may still make sense when the sealed system is intact, parts are available, warranties still matter, and the quote is reasonable next to a new refrigerator of that model. Replacement may win if the compressor has failed, repairs keep repeating, or parts and coverage do not justify another repair. You get a clear price before work begins so you can decide without pressure.
Food-safety temperatures

Keep the refrigerator at or below 40°F and the freezer at or below 0°F. An appliance thermometer is the surest way to know. The [FDA's food storage guidance](https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/are-you-storing-food-safely) uses those targets.

These two time limits are not the same rule. If perishable refrigerated foods such as meat, poultry, fish, eggs, or leftovers have been held above 40°F for more than two hours, discard them. The [FDA's power-outage food safety page](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-during-emergencies/power-outages-key-tips-consumers-about-food-safety) states that guidance and also says not to rely on appearance or odor.

A separate outage rule applies when the refrigerator itself loses power but stays closed. The FDA and [USDA FSIS](https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/emergencies/keep-your-food-safe-during-emergencies) say an unopened refrigerator typically keeps food cold for about four hours. After more than four hours without power, discard perishable refrigerated foods. USDA also says never taste food to determine its safety. When in doubt, throw it out.
